{{1922 Midwest Conference football standings}}
The '''1922 Coe Crimson football team''' represented [[Coe College]] as a member of the newly-formed [[Midwest Conference]] (MWC) during the [[1922 college football season]]. Led by ninth-year head coach [[Moray Eby]], the Kohawks compiled a perfect overall record of 7–0 with a mark of 2–0 in conference play, sharing the MWC title with {{cfb link|year=1922|team=Lawrence Vikings|title=Lawrence}} and {{cfb link|year=1922|team=Millikin Big Blue|title=Millikin}}.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Coe Ranks High In Midwest As Curtain Falls |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-coe-college-cosmos/141789827/ |newspaper=The Coe College Cosmos |location=[[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]] |date=November 23, 1922 |page=1 |access-date=February 21, 2024 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Midwest Conference Football Standings |url=https://static.midwestconference.org/custompages/Past%20MWC%20Seasons/Football/1922-31%20fb%20standings.pdf |publisher=[[Midwest Conference]] |access-date=January 26, 2021 }}</ref> The team held every opponent to seven or fewer points, including a 24–0 shutout against [[1922 Iowa State Cyclones football team|Iowa State]], and outscored all opponents by a total of 136 to 20.

Halfback George Collins was the team's leading scorer with seven touchdowns for 42 points. Makeever ranked second with 31 points on three touchdowns, two field goals, and seven extra-point kicks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Collins Leads Coe Scoring: Kohawk Halfbacks top List During Season Schedule|newspaper=The Coe College Cosmos|date=November 23, 1922|page=1|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-coe-college-cosmos-collins-leads-coe/141909606/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Collins sustained a fractured jaw in the second quarter of the final game of the season against Cornell, played the entire second half with the injury, and led the team to a comeback victory. Collins was hailed in ''The Coe College Cosmos'' as "the greatest half-back who ever wore a Crimson uniform."<ref>{{cite news|title=Students Give Injured Player Great Ovation|newspaper=The Coe College Cosmos|date=November 23, 1922|page=1|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-coe-college-cosmos-george-collins/141909935/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

The team played home games at Coe Field in [[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]].

Professor C. W. Perkins first proposed the "Kohawks" fight name during the [[1922 Coe Kohawks football team|1922 season]].<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=November 7, 1922 |title="Kohawks" Name Suggested By Prof. Foe Coe Athletics |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette/141789656/ |access-date=February 21, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Evening Gazette]] |location=[[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]] |page=10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}}}}</ref> It did not go into effect until the 1928 season. The team had previously been called the "Warriors" and the "Crimson".
